Reviewed the diff. This is a hardening change: it wraps three debug-log call sites in `src/python/model/model.py` (`add_file`, `remove_file`, `update_file`) with `sanitize_log_value()` before interpolating a filename into a log message, closing a CWE-117 log-injection path (CRLF/control-character injection via attacker-influenced filenames reaching `self.logger.debug(...)`).

I verified the sanitizer itself (`src/python/common/types.py:17-58`): it escapes CR/LF to literal `\r`/`\n` tokens and hex-escapes all other C0 control characters (0x00–0x1F) plus DEL (0x7F), including ESC (0x1B) which covers ANSI-escape terminal injection. It deliberately leaves the C1 range (0x80–0x9F) unescaped, with a documented rationale (avoiding corruption of legitimate multi-byte UTF-8 filename bytes) — this is a reasonable, intentional tradeoff and not a meaningful bypass of the log-forging/ANSI-injection threat the sanitizer targets, since CR/LF/ESC are the vectors that actually matter for CWE-117 and those are all covered.

I confirmed `sanitize_log_value` is correctly exported (`src/python/common/__init__.py:1`) and correctly imported/applied at all three sites. The two other `logger.debug`/`logger.error` calls left unchanged in this file (`add_listener`, `remove_listener`) contain no interpolated user-controlled data, so they don't need sanitization.

This is a pure tightening change (reduces what can reach the log sink) with no new vulnerability introduced and no identified bypass of the new control. No defects found.

agent_notes: Change type: this is a safe change that adds a control. Three debug-log calls in Model.add_file, remove_file and update_file (src/python/model/model.py:81, 97, 112) now pass the filename through the existing sanitize_log_value helper (src/python/common/types.py:17). That helper escapes CR/LF and other C0 control characters plus DEL, which blocks log injection (CWE-117).

Public API: none of the method signatures, return values or exceptions change. Only the text of the debug log output changes. The membership checks and the ModelError raising use the raw `file.name` / `filename`, not the sanitized string, so model keys and lookups behave exactly as before.

Blast radius: 11 modules import from model.py (controller, auto_queue, model_builder, file_operation_manager, extract dispatch/process, diff, web stream_model and serialize_model). None of them parse these debug strings, so nothing downstream breaks. Only tests that check exact log text could be affected, and the RED commit 7035477 adds tests that expect this new sanitized output.
Import: `sanitize_log_value` is re-exported from src/python/common/__init__.py:1, so the new import resolves and cannot cause a circular import beyond the existing `from common import AppError`.

Type robustness: sanitize_log_value calls `value.replace`, so a non-str name would now raise AttributeError where `.format` used to stringify it. ModelFile names are str by construction throughout the codebase, so this is not a realistic path, and I am not filing it as a finding.
No database, schema or migration implications. No multi-process or cross-instance implications.

findings.fix_hint: Optionally guard with `if self.logger.isEnabledFor(logging.DEBUG):`, or use lazy %-style args together with a sanitizing wrapper; not required.
findings.problem: The code builds the message with `.format(sanitize_log_value(...))` before calling `logger.debug`. So `sanitize_log_value`, which walks the string one character at a time in Python (src/python/common/types.py:51-58), runs on every Model.add_file/remove_file/update_file call, even when the debug level is turned off. The model is rebuilt on every scan cycle, so this adds a per-file, per-character cost on a hot path. Filenames are short, so the cost is probably negligible. pending: profile a scan cycle with a large model (thousands of files) to see whether this cost is measurable.

findings.why_it_matters: This only matters if a model holds a very large number of files and updates often. Otherwise it is cosmetic.
